items.doc: David N. Baker SI-NEA oral history (2)
items.title: David N. Baker — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: There’s also a recording of the Blues on an album called American Diversions by Jenny Spanoghe, who’s, I guess, French or Belgian?

ctx.x: [Baker chuckles] Um-hm, for one other saxophonist. I think there’s a – I don’t think there’s a percussion concerto as such, even though I’ve written a lot of work – at any rate, those are among the concertos that have been written. There are more sonatas than I could begin to count. Of the recorded ones – Anne Akiko Meyers recorded for RCA Victor my Blues for violin and piano. Starker recorded my sonata for cello. More recently – oh, my concerto for cello and orchestra was recorded by – a name that I can’t

remember [Milos Jahoda] – somebody who’s from the London Symphony Orchestra [the Czech National Symphony Orchestra]. It was recorded with the National Czech Orchestra [the Czech National Symphony Orchestra] and it’s going to be out very soon. There’s also a recording of the Blues on an album called American Diversions by Jenny Spanoghe, who’s, I guess, French or Belgian?
